midnight-ink.$description: Midnight Ink — Page canvas, card backgrounds, primary surface — the near-black base that absorbs everything else

slate-depth.$description: Slate Depth — Elevated surface for buttons and interactive containers, one step above the canvas

steel-edge.$description: Steel Edge — Primary border color, link underlines, nav separators — defines structural edges at very high frequency

graphite-plate.$description: Graphite Plate — Secondary card surface, subtle elevation tier above Midnight Ink

slate-mist.$description: Slate Mist — Muted body text, helper copy, secondary labels — readable but recessive

ash-light.$description: Ash Light — Icon fills, tertiary text, nav inactive states — the lightest non-white neutral

pale-mist.$description: Pale Mist — Light-section borders, hairline dividers, outlines on light backgrounds

cloud.$description: Cloud — Lightest neutral border, soft dividers in light sections

paper.$description: Paper — Light-section canvas, primary text on dark, inverted surface — dual-role neutral

signal-blue.$description: Signal Blue — Primary action fill, brand-action emphasis — the only saturated button color, single violet-blue signal against the dark canvas

status-violet.$description: Status Violet — Violet text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases

deep-teal.$description: Deep Teal — Accent hue in gradient washes, illustrative moments, secondary brand color in art; Brand gradient wash for decorative sections, hero accents, and section backgrounds

amber-glow.$description: Amber Glow — Warm accent in gradient compositions and illustrative highlights — the yellow stop in tri-color gradients

inter.$description: Sole typeface across every role. Inter is chosen for its monospace-adjacent neutrality — it doesn't compete with the device mockups that dominate the page. The aggressive negative tracking on display sizes (-0.021em at 88px) tightens headlines into dense blocks of type that feel machined rather than editorial. Weight 500 is the workhorse for UI; 700 is reserved for primary headlines and emphasis. No serif, no display face — the system is deliberately sans-only and mono-personality.
